discrepancy_1_event_precision.issue: Phase 7 baseline event precision reported as 6.67% in text vs 25.00% in comparison table
discrepancy_1_event_precision.root_cause: Conflation of evaluation domains. In Phase 7's historical script (evaluate_phase7_event_level.py), the evaluation loop over label==0 iterated through all 203 rows of phase7_independent_eval_manifest.csv, which included both the 200 discrete 5-second snippets AND the 3 1-hour continuous streams. The 3 continuous streams produced ~42 false alert events, which were summed into discrete false alerts (14 FP from snippets + 42 FP from streams = 56 FP), yielding TP/(TP+FP) = 4 / (4 + 56) = 6.67%. In Phase 8, discrete evaluation properly excluded continuous streams (leaving 12 FP on discrete snippets), yielding 4 / (4 + 12) = 25.00%. Both numbers are mathematically correct under their respective denominators, but reporting them side-by-side without labeling conflated discrete-snippet precision with hybrid continuous-stream precision.

discrepancy_2_continuous_alerts.issue: Continuous false alerts variously reported as 39 or 42 across three hours (13 vs 14 alerts/hour)
discrepancy_2_continuous_alerts.root_cause: Two distinct 3-hour continuous benchmarks exist in the repository. 1. The Phase 7 Continuous Benchmark comprised: Urban Traffic & Sirens (8 alerts) + Thunderstorm & Rain (13 alerts) + Fireworks & Celebration (21 alerts) = 42 alerts (14.0 alerts/hr). 2. In Phase 8, acquire_phase8_final_dataset.py synthesized a new multi-environment benchmark: Stream 1 Urban Transit & Sirens (10 alerts) + Stream 2 Domestic Interior Transients (0 alerts) + Stream 3 Outdoor Natural Ambience (29 alerts) = 39 alerts (13.0 alerts/hr). The Phase 8 report cited 42 when referring to the historical Phase 7 continuous test, and 39 when evaluating the Phase 7 frozen baseline against the new Phase 8 continuous audio files.

discrepancy_3_final_benchmark_precision.issue: Phase 8 reports 31 true positives and 52 total predicted events, implying 59.62% precision

discrepancy_4_detection_delay_vs_latency.issue: Report cites mean detection delay of 7.2 ms in one table, yet end-to-end streaming delay is 849-935 ms
discrepancy_4_detection_delay_vs_latency.root_cause: Conflation of two completely different physical quantities using the single word 'delay': 1. Algorithmic Onset Delta (7.2 ms): In scripts/evaluate_event_level.py, 'delay' is defined as max(0.0, (det_start_sec - gt_start_sec) * 1000.0). This measures offline timestamp annotation alignment. Because detection windows start prior to or near the physical onset, the offline timestamp offset is near 0 ms. 2. Live Streaming Delivery Latency (849-935 ms): In live streaming audio, detection cannot happen instantaneously. The physical system must buffer 480 ms of new audio (hop duration), execute neural inference on CPU (152 ms), and account for the 960 ms analysis window. The actual live alert reaches the user ~850 ms after sound occurs. Calling offline onset delta 'detection delay' without explicitly stating it is NOT streaming latency was misleading.

discrepancy_5_identical_validation_metri.issue: Candidates B, C, and D yielded identical validation metrics (Recall 71.23%, Precision 94.55%, FP 3)
discrepancy_5_identical_validation_metri.root_cause: A dual pipeline failure: 1. Pipeline Parameter Passthrough Bug: In model_phase8.py (line 304), evaluate_waveform() hardcoded 'allow_short_clip_exception=True' when calling merge_detection_windows_adaptive(), ignoring the candidate configuration. 2. Validation Dataset Distribution Gap: In the historical validation split (102 files), there was only 1 gunshot file shorter than 1.05 seconds (lucadialessandro-shooting-sound-fx-159024.mp3, 0.16s), which had an ensemble score < 0.40 and was missed under ALL configurations. Furthermore, the 86 validation negative files contained zero thunder or fireworks. Therefore, neither the short-clip pathway nor the semantic mimic gating rule was ever stimulated on validation data! Candidates B, C, and D thus performed identically on that split, masking architectural differences until evaluated on the independent benchmarks (where short clips and mimics actually exist).

discrepancy_6_accounting_consistency.issue: Verification of whether windows, events, files, and streams are counted consistently

audit_findings.window_level: Window slicing consistently uses 0.96s window (15,360 samples) and 0.48s hop (7,680 samples). Verified across dataset.py, feature_extractor.py, and model.py.
audit_findings.event_matching_tolerance: Onset matching tolerance varies between scripts: evaluate_phase7_event_level.py used tolerance_sec=0.75, whereas evaluate_phase8_final_system.py used tolerance_sec=0.50. This tightened matching in Phase 8.
audit_findings.duplicate_alerts: Duplicate alerts are correctly excluded from True Positives across all scripts. Once a ground-truth event is matched by an alert, subsequent alerts falling within the same interval are categorized as duplicate_alerts.
audit_findings.file_boundaries: Offline evaluation processes files independently, resetting the streaming buffer and refractory cooldown at file boundaries. This causes short files to truncate earlier than continuous streams.
audit_findings.continuous_stream_treatment: In Phase 7, 3 1-hour continuous streams were lumped into the discrete manifest. In Phase 8, they were isolated into a dedicated continuous audio benchmark. Phase 9 will strictly standardize this separation.
